To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
dietary factors are associated with oxidative DNA damage in women at high risk of breast cancer.
the oxidative DNA damage levels in the blood from women at increased risk for breast cancer were associated with their dietary intakes of meat, fruits, and vegetables.

oxidative DNA damage levels in peripheral blood from women at increased risk for breast cancer were positively associated with dietary intaks of red and processed meats, and inversely associated with dietary intak of vegetables and fruits.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel, low-cost, and high-performance method to detect the DNA damage induced by oxidative stress in human peripheral blood cells.

the development of a new generation of catalysts for the oxidative dehydrogenation of ethane to ethylene, a process that is of considerable industrial importance and which is also relevant to the development of new routes to the production of ethylene from methane.

the development and application of new methods for the detection of DNA adducts in human tissues and the use of these methods to investigate the role of environmental factors and genetic susceptibility in the development of cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of the dietary intake of vegetables and fruits is associated with a reduced risk of breast cancer.
the use of the antioxidant vitamins A, C, and E in the prevention and treatment of breast cancer has been shown not to be effective.
a high consumption of red meats and processed meats is associated with an increased risk of breast cancer, while a high consumption of poultry is associated with a decreased risk.

The main takeaway from our work is that
dietary intake of fruits and vegetables may protect against oxidative stress and DNA damage, and therefore may help to prevent cancer.
the oxidative damage to DNA is a biomarker of cancer risk.
